SAF produced outside of New England is expected to be delivered pre-blended due to existing production volumes, terminal space constraints, infrastructure availability, and limitations in the ability of some terminals to receive fuel by multiple modes. Deliveries of SAF/Jet A blends result in business as usual for New England jet fuel infrastructure, where the same terminals receive the pre-blended fuel delivered by the same barges, tankers, trucks, and pipelines as are used today. The infrastructure investment to handle SAF would occur upstream of New England. There are two primary options for delivery of SAF/Jet A blends. • SAF and Jet A are blended at a Gulf Coast terminal and shipped on the Colonial Pipeline to a New York Harbor terminal. The SAF/Jet A blend is delivered by barge or tanker to New England terminals. BTV received their first shipment SAF/Jet A blend in April 2025, and their fixed-base operator confirmed that the fuel was blended in Texas, 35 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. delivered to a New York Harbor-area terminal by pipeline, and delivered by truck to BTV (Business Air News 2025). LaGuardia International Airport received a SAF/Jet blend from a Texas-based terminal via Colonial Pipeline and Buckeye Partners’ pipeline in 2022 (Neste 2022). • Another option is to blend SAF and Jet A at a New York Harbor terminal. Terminals in New York Harbor tend to be larger and provide greater flexibility to receive and offload fuels by more modes. A previous study funded by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey identified several options for blending SAF and Jet A (Moriarty, Milbrandt, and Tao 2021). Appendix B provides details on New York Harbor terminals storing Jet A. If SAF production significantly increases, there would be potential to deliver SAF and Jet A separately by barge or tanker to New England terminals for blending and delivery to airports.
